LCD1602 Status Panel

Use an I²C backpack to control a 16 × 2 character display and design useful messages within a very small interface.

See ESP32-S3 connectionsStudy the code extract
LevelIntermediate
Suggested time2–3 hours
FocusI²C interface
DeliverableWorking demonstration

01 · Engineering foundation

Know what the circuit is doing.

Parallel display, serial adapter

The HD44780 display normally uses several control and data lines. A PCF8574 backpack converts I²C commands into those parallel signals.

Address variants

Common backpack addresses are 0x27 and 0x3F, but they are not guaranteed. Scan the bus instead of guessing.

Voltage compatibility

Many backpacks are powered from 5 V and pull SDA/SCL up to that supply. ESP32-S3 is a 3.3 V device, so verify pull-up voltage and use level shifting when necessary.

02 · Connections

Wire it to the ESP32-S3.

Before applying power

Do not assume that a 5 V-powered backpack is automatically safe for ESP32-S3 signal pins. Measure or inspect the pull-ups; keep SDA and SCL at 3.3 V logic.

03 · Code focus

Study the important pattern.

#include <Wire.h>
#include <LiquidCrystal_I2C.h>

LiquidCrystal_I2C lcd(0x27, 16, 2);

Wire.begin(8, 9);
lcd.init();
lcd.backlight();
lcd.setCursor(0, 0);
lcd.print("System ready");
lcd.setCursor(0, 1);
lcd.print("Value: ");

This is an instructional extract, not the complete project. Error handling, library setup, and supporting functions may be omitted deliberately.

04 · Project outcome

What a successful build demonstrates.

  • Discover the backpack address
  • Initialise a 16 × 2 display
  • Place content using row and column coordinates
  • Design a two-line status message without unreadable scrolling

05 · Diagnose

Use symptoms as evidence.

SymptomFirst checks
Backlight on, no charactersAdjust the contrast trimmer and verify address and library configuration.
Blocks appear on first lineThe display has power but is not being initialised correctly; check SDA/SCL and address.
ESP32 becomes unstableCheck for 5 V pull-ups on SDA/SCL and correct the interface voltage.

06 · Extend

Move beyond the first demonstration.

  • Create custom characters
  • Build a reaction-time game
  • Add a button-driven menu
  • Compare fixed-width LCD layout with OLED graphics

Equipment

What you need

  • ESP32-S3 development board
  • LCD1602 display
  • PCF8574-based I²C backpack
  • Four jumper wires
  • Optional logic-level shifter depending on the backpack
